questions.question: Explain, with an example, how three business functions depend on each other.
questions.expected_answer: Example: marketing wins an order for 200 desks; production can only make them if purchasing buys enough timber of the right quality; purchasing can only buy if financing has arranged cash or credit. If any one fails, the order fails. General management coordinates them and resolves conflicts.

questions.question: What does an organogram show? Define chain of command and span of control.
questions.expected_answer: An organogram is a diagram of positions and departments joined by lines of authority. It shows levels of management, who reports to whom and formal communication channels. Chain of command: the line of authority from top management down to workers. Span of control: the number of people reporting directly to one manager.

questions.question: Compare how a small and a large business perform the business functions.
questions.expected_answer: Small business: the owner performs most functions personally, some informally or outsourced; quick decisions and low costs, but overload and neglect of functions such as administration and risk management. Large business: separate specialist departments; expertise and capacity, but higher costs, slower decisions and a risk of departments working in silos, so coordination by general management is essential.
